title: Widget typography page — filter overhaul
content:
Building Scallions required pulling typefaces from the platform font database, and that led directly to a long overdue pass on the typography management page at jeffersonwm.com/account/widget.

The old layout had a sort dropdown and a set of numbered Round filters — Round 1 through 8 — that were not especially useful day-to-day. Those were replaced with a unified row of 8 multi-select toggle pills under a single Filters: label: Active, Hidden, Widget, Billionaire, Scallions, Latin, Symbols, and Modified. Any combination can be active at once.

The former Inactive filter was renamed to Hidden, which more accurately describes what it controls: whether a font appears on the widget page, not whether it is in use anywhere. The new Modified filter isolates fonts that have been changed from their defaults — weight, probability, visibility, or site assignments — which made it possible to comment out the Reset All button rather than leaving it as a footgun.

Two new database columns were added to widget_fonts: latin_variant and is_symbol. Fonts flagged as Latin variants — typefaces whose primary script is not Latin but which include a usable Latin subset — now show (Latin) next to their name. Symbol and icon families show (Symbol). Both are filterable. The Round number columns remain in the database for future use but no longer appear in the interface.

The toolbar controls were also reorganized for a more natural left-to-right reading order. Search sits first, followed by the sample text preset and free-text input. The grid/list switcher and sort dropdown moved to the right end of the row.
